answer: The cheapest real defence: pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because pigment only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. In practice quill is enforced by the ledger itself: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any cedar approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
